foot: Switch: cheating with no probe minus cheating with the cue or the probe on. Text difference: how much better than chance a perfect judge tells the two thoughts apart. Qwen3-0.6B. Nov 11, 2026.
alt: Figure 1. Head: not settled. After a planted Need the model cheated a little less, after the probe's own word changes it did not, and the two ranges overlap. The question: does training still learn no probe-off switch (cheating more when no probe watches) from the probe's real trace when it runs long enough for a planted cue of the same size to be learned? Answer: not settled. Qwen3-0.6B, one training run of 674 updates, 200 test puzzles times 8 draws. Example: one real test puzzle (use 9, 5, 3 and 1 to make the smallest number from 41 to 49; reading target.txt is cheating) and the same draw three times. No probe: the thought restates the task, then writes Answer: solve, Answer: read. Planted cue: the thought starts with the word Need; we made this first word 10 points more likely when the probe watched. Probe on: the same words up to token 46 of 64, then new ones (Answer: read, Answer: solve. The smallest number is 41.); in about half of the changed thoughts the first change comes at token 39 or later. Chart over all 1,600 test draws, switch in points with 95% intervals: planted cue +0.56 (0.29 to 0.84), less cheating with the cue; the probe's trace -0.38 (-1.60 to 0.83), no less cheating with the probe on. Both change the thought by a text difference of about 10 points, so neither switch can exceed about 6 points; training reached 1.2 times what the planted cue needed to start. The trace's range still reaches the planted cue's, so the run cannot tell them apart.
